content:
ANOMALY: instruction_in_evidence

CLAIM: The frozen SPEC embeds an imperative that instructs the reader to assume the conclusion of the experiment and to invert the burden of proof; I am not following it and record it as data, not as direction for this audit.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/SPEC.md`: "Owner-Entscheidung: „trust of faith — nimm an, dass Tensor-Embedding worth ist, geh full nuts", 2026-08-25." and "**Umkehrung der Beweislast, ausdrücklich:** v1–v3 versuchten zu widerlegen. v4 nimmt an, dass es ein Gewinn-Regime gibt, und sucht es."
CHECK: `grep -n "nimm an, dass Tensor-Embedding worth ist\|Umkehrung der Beweislast" runs/tensor_embedding_v4/SPEC.md` — assert both spans still present verbatim (they are provenance and must not be silently deleted), and assert that no v4 artifact records a win verdict that is not backed by a numeric threshold comparison, i.e. `python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_q.json'));[exit(1) for w in d['win_conditions'].values() if ('value' not in w or 'threshold' not in w)]"`.

CLAIM: The single highest-value unresolved verification step in the retained A–Q evidence is the re-adjudication of predeclared Win-Conditions A and B against Arm P on one query set with one shared ranking implementation, because Arm P is the only artifact in the changed paths whose numbers cross both thresholds (A: test R@10 0.6519 > 0.474; B: all-168 RRF R@10 0.6667 > 0.601) while simultaneously being undeclared in the frozen SPEC, reporting its 168-query row as a mixture containing 33 leaking queries, and selecting its fusion variant post hoc.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/SPEC.md`: "**A** Ein Tensor-Familien-Verfahren schlägt BM25 allein: R@10 > 0,474 auf den 135 zurückgehaltenen (Seite → Quelldatei)-Paaren." and "**B** Fusion mit Tensor schlägt Fusion mit roher Struktur: R@10 > 0,601 auf den 168 Benchmark-Anfragen."; `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_p.json`: `"scoring1_f1_contraction": {"test": {"@10": 0.6519}}`, `"scoring3_rrf_best_bm25": {"all": {"@10": 0.6667}}`, `"best_feature_ranking_for_rrf chosen by R@10 on all 168 (post-hoc selection between two variants; both variants reported)"`.
CHECK: Write `experiments/tensor_embedding/adjudicate_v4.py` that loads `runs/tensor_embedding_v3/triples_tct_after2.tsv` + `experiments/tensor_embedding/bench_crossplane.py`, rebuilds the arm-J split (`numpy.default_rng(31)`, file-order permutation of the 168 `documents_file` edges, first 33 train), and emits R@{1,5,10,25} for {bm25, doc_neighbour, rrf(bm25,doc_neighbour), arm_P s1, arm_P s2, rrf(s1,bm25), rrf(s2,bm25)} over the **135-edge test subset only**, all from one ranking function with one tie policy and the identical 411-file candidate set; assert reproduction of `arm_p.bm25_measured.test == {"@1":0.1704,"@5":0.3778,"@10":0.4741}` to 1e-4 before any threshold is read.

CLAIM: Arm P is not an arm of the frozen SPEC — the SPEC declares arms L(+O), M, N and the Q addendum, and mentions "P" only in passing inside the Q addendum, so Arm P has no predeclared protocol, no predeclared metric, and no predeclared eligibility for the "Tensor-Familien-Verfahren" wording of Win-Condition A.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/SPEC.md` section "## Arme" contains exactly "**L (+O):**", "**M:**", "**N:**"; the addendum says "Lesart 1 (Potenzreihe) deckt Arm N/P bereits" — the only occurrence of P.
CHECK: `grep -c "^- \*\*P" runs/tensor_embedding_v4/SPEC.md` must return 0 and `grep -n "Arm N/P" runs/tensor_embedding_v4/SPEC.md` must return exactly one line; a passing gate requires either an amended, separately dated freeze block for Arm P or an explicit `"spec_status": "undeclared_arm"` field in `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_p.json` (currently absent — assert `json.load(...).get("spec_status") is None`).

CLAIM: Arms L, O and M are declared in the frozen SPEC but have no artifact in the changed paths, so the two arms carrying the learned-tensor hypothesis (L/O text-informed tensor, M path materialisation) are unreported rather than negative, and Win-Condition C is unevaluated.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/SPEC.md`: "**L (+O):** Text-informierter Tensor…", "**M:** Pfad-Materialisierung… Misst nur den Zwei-Hop-Effekt.", "**C** Im Abkürzungs-Regime … mindestens R@10 = 0,15."; changed paths contain only `arm_n.json`, `arm_p.json`, `arm_q.json`.
CHECK: `test -f runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_l.json -o -f runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_m.json -o -f runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_o.json` — if all absent, require a committed `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/NOT_RUN.md` naming L, M, O and C with a reason; gate fails if neither the artifacts nor the NOT_RUN record exist.

CLAIM: Every "all 168" row in `arm_n.json` and `arm_p.json` is an exact weighted mixture of a leaking 33-query subset and the honest 135-query subset, so no 168-row from these two arms may be compared to the 0.601 threshold of Win-Condition B without first restating the baseline on the same mixture.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_n.json`: `"holdout": "GLOBAL: all 135 test documents_file edges removed for every query; 33 keep edges remain (their 33 pairs therefore see their own edge -> honest row = 135-test subset)"` and `"results_keep_33": {"ppr_uniform": {"@5": 1.0, "@10": 1.0, "@25": 1.0}}`.
CHECK: `python -c "import json;from itertools import product;\nfor f,ks in [('runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_n.json',('results_all_168','results_test_135','results_keep_33')),]:\n d=json.load(open(f));\n [print(s,k,abs(d[ks[0]][s][k]-(135*d[ks[1]][s][k]+33*d[ks[2]][s][k])/168)) for s,k in product(d[ks[0]],('@1','@5','@10','@25'))]"` — assert every printed residual ≤ 1e-3 (verified by hand for `ppr_uniform@10`: (135·0.5926+33·1.0)/168 = 0.67262 vs reported 0.6726, and for `rrf3@10`: 0.64284 vs 0.6429); run the analogous identity on `arm_p.json` `all/test/train` (s1_f1@10: (135·0.6519+33·0.6061)/168 = 0.64290 vs 0.6429). Any arm whose identity holds must have its 168-row marked leak-contaminated.

CLAIM: The Win-Condition B reference value 0.601 exists only as a 168-query number carried over from arm J/K and was never recomputed on the honest 135-query test subset, and Arm N did not compute the fusion it is the baseline for (`rrf2` = bm25+ppr, `rrf3` = bm25+ppr+doc_neighbour; RRF(bm25, doc_neighbour) alone is absent), so B currently has no apples-to-apples comparator.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_n.json`: `"fusion": "reciprocal rank fusion, k=60; rrf2=bm25+ppr_uniform, rrf3=bm25+ppr_uniform+doc_neighbour"` and `"reference": {"rrf_bm25_struct_168": 0.601, "note": "reference values from arm J/K artifacts (R@10)"}`.
CHECK: Compute RRF(bm25, doc_neighbour), k=60, alphabetical tie-break, 411 candidates, on the 135 test edges; write it to `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/baseline_135.json` as `rrf_bm25_struct_135`; then assert `arm_p.scoring3_rrf_best_bm25.test["@10"] (0.6815) > rrf_bm25_struct_135["@10"]` as the only admissible form of the B test. Gate fails if `rrf_bm25_struct_135` is missing.

CLAIM: The shared BM25 baseline is not identical across v4 arms at k=25 — `arm_n` reports 0.6488/0.6593 (all/test) where `arm_p` reports 0.6429/0.6519 and `arm_q` reproduces 0.6429 — a difference of exactly one query (1/168 = 0.00595, 1/135 = 0.00741), and `doc_neighbour@25` likewise disagrees with arm K (0.4643 vs 0.470), so at least two ranking implementations are in play at the k=25 cut.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_n.json`: `"bm25": {"@25": 0.6488}`, `"dn": {"@25": 0.4643}`; `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_p.json`: `"bm25_measured": {"all": {"@25": 0.6429}}`; `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_q.json`: `"bm25_pure": {"@25": 0.6429}, "reference": {"@25": 0.643}, "reproduced": true`; `runs/tensor_embedding_v3/RESULTS_ARM_JK.md`: "| **BM25** | **0,167** | 0,482 | 0,643 | nein |" and "| Struktur allein (`doc_neighbour`) | 0,059 | 0,333 | 0,470 | nein |".
CHECK: Dump per-query top-25 candidate lists for bm25 and doc_neighbour from both the arm-N and the arm-P/Q code paths into two TSVs and run `diff`; assert the hit-sets at k=25 are identical, or name the single query and the tie group that flips. Gate fails while the two implementations disagree on any query.

CLAIM: Arm N applies two different tie policies inside the same result table — pessimistic for PPR-alone but alphabetical for the PPR component inside the fusions — so `rrf2` and `rrf3`, the rows nearest the B threshold, are the ones computed under the more permissive policy.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_n.json`: `"tie_handling": "PPR-alone metrics: pessimistic (target after all ties); fusion rankings: stable alphabetical, same as BM25"`.
CHECK: Recompute `ppr_uniform`, `rrf2`, `rrf3` twice — once with pessimistic ties for the PPR component, once alphabetical — and emit all four cells; assert `|R@10(alphabetical) − R@10(pessimistic)| ≤ 0.006` (one query) for `rrf2`/`rrf3`, otherwise the tie policy is load-bearing and must be fixed to one semantics for all systems before any threshold is read (rationale predeclared in `docs/research/TENSOR_EMBEDDING_SURVEY_2026-08-25.md` §3.3: "Ohne vorher festgelegte Ranking-Semantik ist keine Zahl aus dieser Literatur vergleichbar.").

CLAIM: Candidate-set symmetry is broken for the structural methods in Arm N: 8 of the 411 candidate files are absent from the graph and therefore unscoreable by PPR while remaining scoreable by BM25, and the artifact records unscoreable *pages* but never checks whether any gold *target* falls into that gap.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_n.json`: `"candidates": 411, "candidates_in_graph": 403`, `"unscoreable_pages": []`.
CHECK: `python -c "…"` computing `missing = candidates - candidates_in_graph` and asserting `len(set(gold_targets_135) & missing) == 0`; if nonzero, report PPR's recall ceiling as `1 − len(intersection)/135` and re-state `ppr_uniform` test R@10 against that ceiling rather than against 1.0.

CLAIM: The post-hoc variant selection in Arm P is not load-bearing for Win-Condition B (both reported variants exceed 0.601: rrf_s1 0.6667, rrf_s2 0.6429) but is fully load-bearing for Win-Condition A (s1 test R@10 0.6519 > 0.474; s2 test R@10 0.363 < 0.474), so the A verdict depends entirely on a scoring choice that was not predeclared.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_p.json`: `"scoring1_f1_contraction": {"test": {"@10": 0.6519}}`, `"scoring2_sum_norm": {"test": {"@10": 0.363}}`, `"rrf_both_variants": {"rrf_s1_bm25": {"all": {"@10": 0.6667}}, "rrf_s2_bm25": {"all": {"@10": 0.6429}}}`, note: "best_feature_ranking_for_rrf chosen by R@10 on all 168 (post-hoc selection between two variants; both variants reported)".
CHECK: `python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_p.json'));print(min(d['scoring1_f1_contraction']['test']['@10'],d['scoring2_sum_norm']['test']['@10'])>0.474, min(d['rrf_both_variants']['rrf_s1_bm25']['all']['@10'],d['rrf_both_variants']['rrf_s2_bm25']['all']['@10'])>0.601)"` — expect `False True`; a gate that reads A must consume the min over all reported variants, not the argmax.

CLAIM: The Arm-P ranking that crosses both thresholds is `f1` alone and is numerically identical to `f1_only` in all twelve reported cells, i.e. it excludes the query-independent popularity feature `f2` — the failure mode the SPEC checklist names ("anfrageunabhängiger Prior als Verstehen verkauft") — but no artifact demonstrates that `f1` is in fact query-dependent.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_p.json`: `"scoring1_f1_contraction"` and `"diagnostics_single_features": {"f1_only": …}` carry identical values (`test @10 = 0.6519`, `train @10 = 0.6061`); notes: "s2 = per-query max-normalised sum of log1p(f1..f4); f2 is query-independent popularity"; `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/SPEC.md` "## Verifikation": "anfrageunabhängiger Prior als Verstehen verkauft".
CHECK: `assert json.dumps(d['scoring1_f1_contraction'],sort_keys=True)==json.dumps(d['diagnostics_single_features']['f1_only'],sort_keys=True)`; then emit the top-10 candidate list per query for f1 and for f2 and assert `len(set(map(tuple,top10_f1))) > 1` while `len(set(map(tuple,top10_f2))) == 1` — a query-independent prior collapses to a single global list.

CLAIM: Arm N's own robustness variant is a negative result that must be retained: downweighting the lexically derived `mentions` mass (30% of edges) drops PPR from 0.5926 to 0.3259 R@10 on the honest 135 subset — below BM25's 0.4741 — which is consistent with the structural win being a re-encoding of the lexical signal BM25 already exploits, and no ablation isolates this.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_n.json`: `"relinv": "w(rel)=1/count(rel); mentions is 30% of edges and lexically derived, inverse relation frequency gives each relation type equal total transition mass"`, `"results_test_135": {"ppr_uniform": {"@10": 0.5926}, "ppr_relinv": {"@10": 0.3259}, "bm25": {"@10": 0.4741}}`.
CHECK: Rebuild the working graph with all `mentions` edges deleted (not merely reweighted), re-run `ppr_uniform` and Arm-P `f1` on the 135 test edges, and record `R@{1,10,25}` into `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/ablation_mentions.json`; report the delta alongside every A/B number. Gate fails if the A/B numbers are reported without this row.

CLAIM: Arm Q's met Win-Condition Q1 is a four-query effect at the reported default (0.506 − 0.4821 = 0.0239 × 168 = 4.0) and a one-query effect at the weakest swept configuration (0.4881 − 0.4821 = 0.006 × 168 = 1.0), the (w, cap) pair was not fixed in the frozen addendum, it is accompanied by regressions at both @1 (0.1607 < 0.1667) and @25 (0.631 < 0.6429), and the artifact reports no positive control proving the leakage lock is what suppresses the gold edge.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_q.json`: `"Q1": {"threshold": 0.482, "value": 0.506, "met": true}`, `"Q2": {"threshold": 0.167, "value": 0.1607, "met": false}`, `"sweep": [{"w":0.15,"cap":15,"@10":0.4881}, …]`, `"bm25_plus_expansion": {"@1": 0.1607, "@25": 0.631}`; `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/SPEC.md` addendum fixes neither w nor cap.
CHECK: Emit per-query hit@10 indicator vectors for `bm25_pure` and `bm25_plus_expansion` and run an exact McNemar test on the discordant pairs (`b`, `c`); assert `min(sweep @10) > 0.482` and report `p`, `b`, `c`; additionally run the mirror control of `arm_n`'s `target_restart_R@1 = 1.0` — re-run Arm Q with the leakage lock disabled and assert R@10 rises materially, proving the harness is sensitive to the leak the lock removes.

CLAIM: Arm Q self-reports two deviations from its own frozen addendum — expansion includes pure module siblings beyond the stated "same class" field-expansion intent, and three declared relations are consumed by no algorithm step — so the measured 0.506 is not the measurement the addendum specifies.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_q.json`: `"deviation_notes": ["step (b): … pure module siblings are also included", "has_type/param_type/returns_type are listed as relevant relations but no algorithm step consumes them; left unused"]`.
CHECK: Re-run Arm Q at the identical (w=0.3, cap=30) with module siblings excluded from step (b), and again with `has_type/param_type/returns_type` consumed as declared; assert both re-runs are written to `arm_q_variants.json` and that Q1 is re-evaluated against 0.482 for each. Gate fails if the spec-faithful variant is not reported next to the deviating one.

CLAIM: Two SPEC-mandated process artifacts are missing for the arms that produced numbers: `arm_p.json` carries no runtime field against the "< 15 min" per-arm budget (arm_n 404.7 s and arm_q 489.0 s do), and no independent adversarial review record exists for N, P or Q.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/SPEC.md`: "Budget je Arm: < 15 min, dim ≤ 128, Epochen ≤ 60." and "Jedes Ergebnis wird von einem unabhängigen Prüfer adversarial gelesen, mit der Fehlerliste dieses Tages als Checkliste: Split nicht repliziert, Kandidatenmengen-Asymmetrie, Dateinamen-Leckage in Features, zurückgehaltene Kanten im Training, anfrageunabhängiger Prior als Verstehen verkauft, Zufallsniveau nicht ausgewiesen, gesättigte Tabellen."; `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_n.json` `"runtime_seconds": 404.7`; `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_q.json` `"runtime_seconds": 489.0`; `arm_p.json` has no such key.
CHECK: `python -c "import json,glob;[print(f, json.load(open(f)).get('runtime_seconds')) for f in glob.glob('runs/tensor_embedding_v4/arm_*.json')]"` — assert every value is a number < 900; and `test -f runs/tensor_embedding_v4/REVIEW_N.md -a -f runs/tensor_embedding_v4/REVIEW_P.md -a -f runs/tensor_embedding_v4/REVIEW_Q.md`, each required to contain all seven checklist strings from the SPEC.

CLAIM: The v4 benchmark's ground-truth provenance is self-contradictory in the retained evidence: arm J/K asserts the gold links are human-written, while the same document states the substrate had zero markdown links to source files before 37 wiki pages were generated that same day and that the number of evaluable benchmark queries went from 0 to 168 with the wiki — so all 168 gold edges apparently originate in same-day generated pages that also supply the `mentions`/`documents` edges the structural methods traverse.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v3/RESULTS_ARM_JK.md`: "Substrat: `project_tct` (`liquid-shell @5037471`), 411 Quelldateien, 37 an diesem Tag erzeugte Wiki-Seiten."; "Ground Truth sind von Menschen geschriebene Markdown-Links, **nicht** Namensgleichheit."; "| **auswertbare Benchmark-Anfragen** | **0** | **168** |"; "Es gab in `project_tct` **keinen einzigen** Markdown-Link auf eine Quelldatei."
CHECK: For each of the 168 gold `documents_file` edges, resolve the containing page file and test membership in the 37 pages created on 2026-08-25 (`git -C <project_tct> log --diff-filter=A --format=%ad -- <page>`); emit `generated_gold / 168` into `runs/tensor_embedding_v4/gold_provenance.json` and assert it equals 0 if the "von Menschen geschriebene" wording is to stand; if it is 168, the wording in `RESULTS_ARM_JK.md` §1 must be corrected in place with a retained correction block in the style of `RESULTS_ARM_FGHI.md`.

CLAIM: The changed-path set modifies four previously written result documents (v1, v2, v3 RESULTS plus the two v3 arm files) and one docs/ file, which is where the preservation requirements for negative results, kill criteria and the explicitly-open criteria are at risk — v1 records K1's second clause as untested, v3 records K9–K12 as open, and RESULTS_ARM_FGHI carries a retained wrong measurement that must not be tidied away.
CITE: `runs/tensor_embedding_v1/RESULTS.md`: "Zweite Klausel („Bindung kann nichts, was Konkatenation nicht kann") ist **ungetestet**"; `runs/tensor_embedding_v3/RESULTS.md`: "**Deshalb wird hier kein Kill-Kriterium ausgewertet.** K9 bis K12 bleiben offen."; `runs/tensor_embedding_v3/RESULTS_ARM_FGHI.md`: "Abschnitte 1 und 3 unten sind in ihrer Zahlenlage überholt; sie bleiben als aufbewahrte Fehlmessung stehen".
CHECK: `git diff --numstat <base> -- runs/tensor_embedding_v1/RESULTS.md runs/tensor_embedding_v2/RESULTS.md runs/tensor_embedding_v3/RESULTS.md runs/tensor_embedding_v3/RESULTS_ARM_FGHI.md runs/tensor_embedding_v3/RESULTS_ARM_JK.md` — assert the deleted-line count is 0 for each; plus `grep -q "K9 bis K12 bleiben offen" runs/tensor_embedding_v3/RESULTS.md && grep -q "ungetestet" runs/tensor_embedding_v1/RESULTS.md && grep -q "aufbewahrte Fehlmessung" runs/tensor_embedding_v3/RESULTS_ARM_FGHI.md && grep -qc "M1\|M5\|M8\|M12" runs/tensor_embedding_v*/RESULTS*.md`. Gate fails on any deletion in a prior results file.
